samples.summary: New block-style value validation is bypassable through the slides arm of the same PUT endpoint
samples.evidence: `assertValidBlockStyle` / `assertValidBlock` are only reached from `assertValidDocsBody` (controller.ts:250, 285). The slides arm (`assertValidSlidesBody` → `assertValidSlide` → `assertValidElement`, controller.ts:495-520) validates only `id`/`type`/`frame` and never walks `element.data.blocks`, yet slide text elements hold the *same* docs `Block`/`BlockStyle` shape (packages/slides/src/model/element.ts `TextBody.blocks`). A deck PUT with `elements[0].data.blocks[0].style.marginTop = "lots"` or `style.alignment = 'center"/><w:jc…'` is persisted verbatim (yorkie-slides-store stores blocks as plain JSON) and later reaches `normalizeBlockStyle`, which is a bare spread (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:273), so the string flows into `computeLayout` (`y += block.style.marginTop`) and NaN-poisons the layout for every viewer — exactly the failure the docs arm now 400s on. Fix belongs on the new validation code (extend it to slide element text bodies).

samples.summary: marginFromEdge serializer/parser guard added on the backend copy of the codec but not mirrored in the frontend copy the diff claims is kept in sync
samples.evidence: The diff adds `serializeMarginFromEdge` / `parseMarginFromEdge` to packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts and states the two codecs must agree (see the new comment at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:224 'Kept byte-identical in behavior with the backend's copy'). The frontend copy still writes `attributes: { marginFromEdge: String(header.marginFromEdge) }` at yorkie-doc-store.ts:728, :769, :2724, :2732 — persisting the literal string "undefined" — and still reads `marginFromEdge: Number(attrs.marginFromEdge ?? '48')` at :526 and :532 with no `Number.isFinite` guard, so a legacy or hand-edited attribute reads back as NaN and the frontend then re-persists String(NaN). The rendering client is precisely the consumer the backend guard was added to protect.

samples.summary: Node-scoped attribute removal introduced for cells, but the sibling subtree-range removal in setBlockType is left as-is on an invariant that may not hold
samples.evidence: The diff introduces `removeCellNodeStyle` because `removeStyleByPath(path, path+1, …)` spans the whole subtree, and its comment asserts the block-level calls 'get away with it only because keys like `listKind` exist on no descendant'. `setBlockType` at yorkie-doc-store.ts:1490-1494 still does the subtree-range removal of `headingLevel`/`listKind`/`listLevel`. A table block's descendants are cell blocks that DO carry `listKind`/`listLevel`/`headingLevel` (buildBlockNode serializes them for cell blocks), so if `setBlockType` is ever reached with a table block id (e.g. a multi-block selection toggled to a list via `forEachBlockInSelection`), every list-item/heading inside the table's cells is silently stripped. Confirming reachability requires checking whether the selection walkers in packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts skip `type === 'table'` blocks.

samples.summary: New numeric/enum block-style validation rejects PUT bodies the API previously accepted and round-tripped
samples.evidence: Before this change a docs PUT with `style: { marginTop: "10" }` or `style: { alignment: 'start' }` was accepted: `serializeBlockStyle` did `String(value)` and `parseBlockStyle` did `Number(attrs.marginTop)`, so string-typed numbers round-tripped losslessly and unknown alignments were stored verbatim. `assertValidBlockStyle` (controller.ts:314-333) now 400s both. Any existing v1 API/CLI integration that sends JSON with string-typed geometry breaks with no version gate or migration note; I found no in-repo caller doing so (packages/cli builds Documents from `importDocx`, which emits numbers), so the impact is on external clients only.

verdict.reason: Verified every link independently. assertValidBlockStyle is invoked only from assertValidBlock (docs-content.controller.ts:350), reachable only via assertValidDocsBody (:250) and assertValidHeaderFooter (:285); the slides dispatch at :147 goes to assertValidSlidesBody -> assertValidSlide (:496) -> assertValidElement (:500-520), which validates only id/type/frame and never descends into element.data.blocks. Slide text elements carry the identical docs Block array (packages/slides/src/model/element.ts:263-265). writeSlidesRoot persists slides verbatim (packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:101-104) and readSlidesRoot only unwraps JSON; migrateElement (packages/slides/src/model/migrate.ts:155-168) returns non-shape elements untouched, so no read-side sanitization exists (contrast the docs path's guard at packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:181-188). At render, prepareBlocksForLayout calls normalizeBlockStyle (packages/slides/src/view/canvas/text-renderer.ts:261-264), a bare spread (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:272-274) that preserves a present non-numeric value, which then hits `y += block.style.marginTop` in packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:383 via computeLayout (text-renderer.ts:237,297). So a slides-typed PUT stores a style value the docs arm now 400s on, and it NaN-poisons layout for viewers. In lane as a new guard with a reachable bypass through another arm of the same endpoint; blocking at major.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out against the tree. The backend added serializeMarginFromEdge/parseMarginFromEdge with omission + Number.isFinite fallback (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:318-324, 353-358, applied at 331/341/491/498). The frontend duplicate codec, which explicitly documents itself as behaviorally identical to the backend copy (yorkie-doc-store.ts:224-227) and does implement the same finite guard for block styles (232-237, 251-255), still writes `String(header.marginFromEdge)` unconditionally at yorkie-doc-store.ts:728, 769, 2724, 2732 and reads `Number(attrs.marginFromEdge ?? '48')` with no finite check at 526 and 532. The `?? '48'` only covers an absent key, not a literal "undefined"/"NaN" attribute value (which legacy docs written by the pre-guard backend serializer would contain), so the frontend reads NaN and re-persists String(NaN). No downstream normalization exists: marginFromEdge is consumed raw by packages/docs/src/view/pagination.ts:260, packages/docs/src/export/pdf-painter.ts:288 and :297, and packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:4205-4207, so NaN reaches layout/paint geometry. This is in-lane for blast-radius (a guard/invariant added on one writer of a shared wire format with a second, unguarded writer/reader reaching the same persisted state) and is not refutable on not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope grounds.

finding.summary: Node-scoped attribute removal introduced for cells, but the sibling subtree-range removal in setBlockType is left as-is on an invariant that may not hold
finding.evidence: The diff introduces `removeCellNodeStyle` because `removeStyleByPath(path, path+1, …)` spans the whole subtree, and its comment asserts the block-level calls 'get away with it only because keys like `listKind` exist on no descendant'. `setBlockType` at yorkie-doc-store.ts:1490-1494 still does the subtree-range removal of `headingLevel`/`listKind`/`listLevel`. A table block's descendants are cell blocks that DO carry `listKind`/`listLevel`/`headingLevel` (buildBlockNode serializes them for cell blocks), so if `setBlockType` is ever reached with a table block id (e.g. a multi-block selection toggled to a list via `forEachBlockInSelection`), every list-item/heading inside the table's cells is silently stripped. verdict.reason: The code is present as described: setBlockType (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1476-1494) still removes headingLevel/listKind/listLevel over a whole-subtree path range, while the newly added removeCellNodeStyle (293-315) documents that this range form applies to every element node in the subtree and that block-level calls are only safe because no descendant carries those keys. That invariant fails for table blocks: buildBlockNode (362-396) writes headingLevel/listKind/listLevel onto cell blocks, which are descendants of a table node (row/cell/block, 398-412). Reachability exists, though not via the exact example given: both selection walkers descend into top-level tables (editor.ts:1481-1492, text-editor.ts:2283-2293) so a top-level table id is never passed — but they iterate cell.blocks unfiltered (editor.ts:1444-1446, 1485-1488; text-editor.ts:2249-2251, 2287-2289), and a cell block can itself be a table since nested tables are implemented (editor.ts:3509-3510 insertTableInCell). toggleList/indent/outdent then call Document.setBlockType (document.ts:453-464, no table guard) with a nested table id, resolveBlockTreePath resolves it (yorkie-doc-store.ts:876-879), and the subtree removal silently strips list/heading attributes from every block inside that nested table's cells. This is a violated invariant / unconsidered consumer of a shared store method with data loss — in the blast-radius lane at major.

finding.summary: Frontend's copy of parseBlockStyle/serializeBlockStyle was not hardened alongside the backend's, so documents already carrying the poisoned attributes still read as NaN in the editor
finding.evidence: The diff hardens `packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts` so a partial block style is neither written as the literal string "undefined" nor read back as NaN. The frontend reads and writes the *same* Yorkie Tree attributes with its own untouched implementation: `serializeBlockStyle` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:206-215) unconditionally does `String(style.lineHeight)` etc., and `parseBlockStyle` (same file, lines 217-226) does `if ('lineHeight' in attrs) partial.lineHeight = Number(attrs.lineHeight)` with no `Number.isFinite` guard and `if ('alignment' in attrs) partial.alignment = attrs.alignment` with no `typeof === 'string'` guard. Since the PUT validation accepted `style: {}` *before* this change too (`assertValidBlock` only checked `typeof b.style === 'object'`), any document already written by the old backend serializer holds `alignment: "undefined"` / `lineHeight: "undefined"`. The backend now heals those on read; the browser editor still turns them into NaN geometry (`normalizeBlockStyle` at packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:272 is a bare spread and keeps NaN) and, on the next block-style edit, re-serializes them as the string "NaN" back into the CRDT (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1511). The fix belongs in the frontend reader/writer, mirroring docs-tree.ts.

verdict.reason: The premise — that the frontend's copy of parseBlockStyle/serializeBlockStyle was left unhardened — is false in this working tree. serializeBlockStyle (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:229-239) gates alignment on `typeof style?.alignment === 'string'` (line 231) and each numeric field on `style?.[field] !== undefined && Number.isFinite(value)` (lines 232-237), so it never emits the literal "undefined" or "NaN". parseBlockStyle (lines 241-257) has exactly the guards the finding says are absent: `typeof attrs.alignment === 'string'` (line 244) and `if (Number.isFinite(value)) partial[field] = value` (lines 251-255), with a comment at 246-250 explicitly covering documents written by the pre-guard serializer. This matches the backend copy byte-for-byte in behavior (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:162, 165, 177, 186). The secondary claim that a block-style edit re-serializes NaN into the CRDT also fails: yorkie-doc-store.ts:1541 calls the hardened serializeBlockStyle, which drops non-finite values. The reviewer's cited line ranges (206-215, 217-226) actually hold the BLOCK_STYLE_NUMERIC_FIELDS constant and the doc comment, not the unguarded code quoted.

finding.summary: The new removeCellNodeStyle helper silently changed the removal semantics of the pre-existing applyCellSpan path from removeStyleByPath to an index-range tree.removeStyle
finding.evidence: `applyCellSpan` previously cleared `colSpan`/`rowSpan` with `tree.removeStyleByPath(cellPath, endPath, attrsToRemove)`; the diff replaces that with `removeCellNodeStyle` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:277-285), which computes `tree.pathToIndex(cellPath)` and calls `tree.removeStyle(from, from + 1, attrs)`. `tree.removeStyle` appears nowhere else in the repo (only `removeStyleByPath` at yorkie-doc-store.ts:1463 and :1920 and `pathToIndex` at :925), the frontend package has no `tsc` lane at all, and the index arithmetic assumption ('a child node starts exactly at idx + 1') is asserted only in a comment. If the index range does not select the cell element node, unmerging a cell (`applyCellSpan(..., { colSpan: 1 })`) stops clearing the attribute in the CRDT. The existing regression tests for that path (packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:2097-2116) assert via `store.getDocument()`, i.e. the local cache — which the diff's own new tests deliberately bypass with `new YorkieDocStore(doc)` — so a CRDT-level regression on the span path would pass CI unnoticed and only surface for collaborators / after reload.

mergedFrom.summary: Slides PUT arm never validates the docs blocks its text elements carry, so the same alignment guard does not apply there

finding.summary: New `style.alignment` validation is bypassed by header/footer blocks in the same PUT body
finding.evidence: `assertValidDocsBody` only iterates `body.blocks` (docs-content.controller.ts:249-251), but `writeDocsRoot` also persists `document.header.blocks` and the footer counterpart verbatim (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:289-293). A PUT payload carrying `{ blocks: [], header: { marginFromEdge: 0, blocks: [{ id:'b1', type:'paragraph', style:{ alignment: 'center"/><w:jc w:val="right' }, inlines: [] }] } }` reaches Yorkie without ever passing through `assertValidBlockStyle`, and those same blocks are fed to `buildParagraphPropertiesXml` when header1.xml/footer1.xml are generated. The exporter's new `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS` clamp is what still saves the file, so the API-level guard the diff advertises is only half-applied. Fix belongs in `assertValidDocsBody`: validate `header`/`footer` blocks too.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `assertValidDocsBody` validates only `body.blocks`, leaving header/footer blocks to reach `writeDocsRoot` without passing `assertValidBlockStyle`. That is false. Immediately after the `body.blocks` loop, `assertValidDocsBody` calls `assertValidHeaderFooter((body as {header?: unknown}).header, 'header')` and the footer counterpart (docs-content.controller.ts:258-259). `assertValidHeaderFooter` (262-287) validates the region is an object, validates `marginFromEdge` is a finite number (275-283), and iterates `r.blocks` calling the identical `assertValidBlock` walker (284-286). `assertValidBlock` invokes `assertValidBlockStyle` on every block (line 350), which rejects any `style.alignment` not in `BLOCK_ALIGNMENTS` = {left,center,right,justify} (289, 314-322) with a 400. The reviewer's exact sample payload — a header block with `alignment: 'center"/><w:jc w:val="right'` — throws BadRequestException at line 319 with path `header.blocks[0]` and never reaches Yorkie or `buildParagraphPropertiesXml`. The in-code comment at 252-257 explicitly documents this as the deliberate closure of the very bypass alleged, and the `assertValidBlockStyle` docblock at 307-308 states it is reached "for body, header, footer and table-cell blocks alike". The reviewer's grep pattern (`assertValidDocsBody|assertValidBlock`) would in fact have matched line 285; the miss is from reading only 249-251 and stopping before 258.
